questions.q: How would you like to be billed?

options.label: By data scanned
options.why: you pay per query on bytes scanned

options.label: By compute time or credits

questions.hint: The tools above store, organize and query data. Loading your databases is a separate job.

options.label: Copied from my databases
options.why: your data starts in a database and you want it copied into Iceberg tables

options.label: It is already files in storage
options.why: your data is already files in object storage

athena.name: Amazon S3 plus Athena
athena.summary: Object storage with a query engine you do not run, billed on data scanned. Lake Formation can add access rules.
athena.bestWhen: you are on AWS and run occasional SQL over files in S3.
athena.watchOut: Athena's docs say it creates and operates only on Iceberg v2 tables, and only tables created against the AWS Glue catalog work.

fabric.name: Microsoft Fabric OneLake
fabric.summary: One lake per Fabric tenant, built on Azure Data Lake Storage, with capacity billed per workspace.
fabric.bestWhen: you use Power BI and want one lake.
fabric.watchOut: Fabric engines store data in Delta Parquet, so Iceberg is bridged rather than the default.

bigquery.name: Google BigQuery
bigquery.summary: A Google Cloud platform with Iceberg managed tables kept in your own buckets, billed per TiB scanned or by slots.
bigquery.bestWhen: your analysts use BigQuery and you want Iceberg files in your own Cloud Storage.
bigquery.watchOut: the docs say only one UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE runs on a table at a time, and renaming, copying and cloning are not supported.

trino.name: Object storage, Iceberg and Trino
trino.summary: Open parts you assemble yourself: cloud storage, the Iceberg format and the free Trino engine.
trino.bestWhen: you have engineers who can run a cluster and want no per-query or platform fee.
trino.watchOut: free software, so engine setup and table upkeep are on your team.

databricks.name: Databricks
databricks.summary: A platform for Spark, SQL and machine learning in one workspace, billed in Databricks Units.
databricks.bestWhen: Spark, SQL and machine learning all live in one team.
databricks.watchOut: managed Iceberg tables need Unity Catalog, Runtime 16.4 LTS or newer and serverless compute, and the per-DBU price may not be the full bill.

snowflake.name: Snowflake
snowflake.summary: A managed SQL engine that works over Iceberg tables in storage you control, billed in credits.
snowflake.bestWhen: your team lives in SQL and wants a managed engine over open files.
snowflake.watchOut: it is a proprietary managed service with no self-hosted option found, and cross-region queries add egress costs.

dremio.name: Dremio
dremio.summary: Self-service SQL on Iceberg, as a managed cloud or a self-managed Enterprise version.
dremio.bestWhen: you want one SQL layer over Iceberg and may want to self-host later.
dremio.watchOut: Dremio Cloud runs on AWS only for now, and the Enterprise price is not published.

olake.name: OLake Go plus a catalog and an engine
olake.summary: Open-source tool that captures changes from Postgres, MySQL and MariaDB, MongoDB and SQL Server (Oracle, Db2, S3 and Kafka load without database change capture) into Iceberg or Parquet on storage you run.
olake.bestWhen: your data starts in a database and you want Iceberg tables that Trino, Athena or another engine can read.
olake.watchOut: OLake Go loads the lake, so you still pick a catalog and a query engine.
